speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what happened right before you lost consciousness, and did you experience any warning signs like dizziness or chest pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you feel any lightheadedness, nausea, or visual changes immediately before standing up to urinate? Also, do you have a history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or heart conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia or difficulty initiating your urinary stream? I suspect this may be a micturition syncope, but I need to rule out cardiac causes. REQUEST TEST: ECG

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal ECG and the classic presentation of syncope immediately following urination with rapid recovery, this is highly suggestive of micturition syncope. To definitively rule out structural heart disease as a contributing factor, I will request an echocardiogram. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Doctor
text: With a normal echocardiogram ruling out structural heart disease, the diagnosis of micturition syncope is confirmed. I recommend staying hydrated and avoiding sudden position changes after waking at night to prevent future episodes. DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition Syncope
